**Wednesday, October 14, 2026 -**_****_

_**Yemen** : Ansarallah claims missile and drone strikes on Saudi Aramco
facilities and Riyadh airport. Saudi Aramco headquarters extensively damaged
in Ansarallah attack. Saudi-led strikes hit oil facilities in Yemen's Hodeidah
and Sana'a, killing two. Yemen hospitals overwhelmed by war casualties as
fighting cuts aid to 800,000 people. Cholera cases surge amid mass
displacement in unsanitary camps._

_**Palestine** : Israeli strike on Gaza City apartment kills Palestinian
woman. Israeli forces uproot olive trees, settlers attack Palestinians across
the occupied West Bank. Over 2,000 Gaza patients die awaiting medical care.
Israeli settlers torch mosque near Jerusalem amid 13 attacks on mosques in
2026. Gaza doctor beaten at prison in front of Israel's Ben Gvir, Palestinian
officials say._

_**Iran** : Three Iranian fishermen seriously injured in drone strike. Iran
reports first ship sinking from naval mine in Strait of Hormuz. Iran carries
out latest execution as UN experts call for halt._

_**Lebanon:** Israel strikes multiple towns across southern Lebanon in
continued ceasefire violations. UN warns Israeli attacks and destruction in
southern Lebanon may amount to war crimes despite ceasefire._

_**U.S.** : Top House Republicans privately concede House control is "all but
gone," shift focus to saving Senate majority. Federal probe of Rep. Ilhan Omar
reportedly centers on birth date and citizenship papers. DOJ gives California
48 hours to act on alleged noncitizen voter list or face legal action. NYC
Comptroller Mark Levine backs off campaign pledge to buy Israeli bonds. ICE
seeks AI software to monitor detainees' calls, video and movements. Trump
pardons two Alaska mechanics on stage at Wasilla rally. CBS analysis: More
than half of top bidders for Trump meme coin dinner appear to be overseas. CVS
to pay $315 million in unlawful opioids settlement. Bank of America fined $1.2
billion over customer money laundering._

_**International:** Ethiopian troops reach Eritrea border, raising war
concerns. India orders temporary jailing of two leaders of Cockroach Janta
Party. Russian strikes kill three people in Kyiv, leave 600,000 without power.
Ukraine hits Russia's largest data center. Pakistan suspends provincial party
of Imran Khan; police assail party supporters. DRC tops 9,000 Ebola cases,
4,300 deaths. U.S. recalls acting envoy to Nicaragua after Ortega government
rejects ambassador nominee. Russia arrests Japanese journalist, claims
"espionage."_

**Correction:** An earlier headline incorrectly referred to the vessel as a
tanker rather than a cargo ship.

**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**

* * *

# Yemen

  * **Ansarallah claims missile and drone strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities and Riyadh airport:** Yemen's Ansarallah [said](https://x.com/yah_saree/status/2110289506410676247?s=46) Wednesday they launched a large-scale attack using ballistic and cruise missiles and drones against Saudi Aramco facilities in Dhahran, in the kingdom's Eastern Province, King Khalid International Airport and an Aramco refinery in Riyadh.

    * The group claimed the strikes caused destruction and fires, threatening further attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities in retaliation for Saudi-led attacks in Yemen. Saudi warplanes carried out 104 airstrikes and missile attacks over the past 24 hours across Sana'a, Dhamar, Taiz, Amran, Lahj, al-Jawf, Marib, Saada, and Hodeidah, causing civilian casualties, according to the group.

    * Saudi Arabia's military coalition separately [announced](https://x.com/cjfcspox/status/2110274605768155532?s=46) it had intercepted and destroyed an Ansarallah ballistic missile targeting the capital, where authorities issued an air-raid alert urging residents to shelter indoors.

    * Four people, including two women, a man, and a child, were [injured](https://x.com/saudidcd/status/2110125628129521900?s=46) in Riyadh by falling debris from two intercepted cruise missiles, which also caused minor damage to 15 homes, according to Saudi's Civil Defense. A separate [interception](https://x.com/saudidcd/status/2110354392927088672?s=46) Wednesday led to the injury of one person and damage to a house and a vehicle.

  * **Saudi Aramco headquarters extensively damaged in Ansarallah attack:** Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran, eastern Saudi Arabia, [suffered](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/aramcos-dhahran-hq-suffered-extensive-damage-tuesdays-attack-sources-say-2026-10-14/) extensive damage in an attack Tuesday, with a fire spreading across several floors, according to Reuters. The top three floors, where CEO Amin Nasser's office is located, were severely damaged, with collapsed ceilings and shattered windows and doors.

    * The fire continued burning into early Wednesday, Reuters reported. Operations at the complex, which houses a control center overseeing oil rigs, refineries, export terminals, and pipelines, have reportedly continued, although some employees were instructed to work from home and certain functions were transferred to global offices. Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry described the fire as limited.

  * **Saudi-led strikes hit oil facilities in Yemen 's Hodeidah and Sana'a, killing two: **Two people were killed and two others wounded in a Tuesday [airstrike](https://apnews.com/article/yemen-houthis-saudi-arabia-strikes-threats-307d49abfe63ff66c99c318d94ca3e15) on a state oil company facility in the Ras Isa port area of Hodeidah province, the Sana'a-based Health Ministry said Wednesday. The Saudi-led coalition also struck a Yemeni Oil Company facility in the Ansarallah-controlled capital, Sana'a, after issuing a warning ordering civilians to evacuate the site and nearby storage areas.

    * The Yemeni Oil Company claimed its storage facilities were empty and that the strike would not affect fuel reserves or supplies.

  * **Yemen hospitals overwhelmed by war casualties as fighting cuts aid to 800,000 people:** Hospitals in Marib, Taiz, and along Yemen's Red Sea coast are [struggling](https://www.icrc.org/en/article/yemen-health-system-faces-mounting-pressure-fighting-intensifies) with unprecedented numbers of war casualties, with some admitting more than 700 wounded patients in a single week, the International Committee of the Red Cross warned Wednesday.

    * Fighting and road closures also cut off humanitarian assistance to around 800,000 people in Taiz and other affected areas, according to the UN World Food Programme. Wheat flour stocks are nearly exhausted, while remaining food supplies in local markets may last only a short time.

  * **Cholera cases surge amid mass displacement in unsanitary camps:** Suspected cholera cases in Yemen have tripled in the past three weeks, rising from 217 cases to 647, [according](https://www.emro.who.int/media/news/cholera-cases-surge-as-conflict-in-yemen-displaces-over-200-000-people.html) to the World Health Organization (WHO). Yemen has reported 8,034 suspected cases of cholera and 27 deaths this year, with a quarter of cases occurring in the last four weeks.

    * Five governorates hosting large numbers of displaced people in the southwest of Yemen--Abyan, Lahj, Al-Dhale'e, Taiz and Aden--accounted for 92% of reported cholera cases.

    * "Escalating conflict and mass displacement in Yemen are increasing the risk of infectious disease outbreaks as overcrowding, inadequate access to safe water and disrupted health services expose growing numbers of people to cholera, measles and other preventable diseases," the WHO said.

# Palestine

  * **Israeli strike on Gaza City apartment kills Palestinian woman:** A Palestinian woman was [killed](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/14/%D8%B4%D9%87%D9%8A%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D9%88%D9%85%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%AC%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D9%82%D8%B5%D9%81-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D8%B4%D9%82%D8%A9-%D8%B3%D9%83%D9%86%D9%8A%D8%A9) in an Israeli airstrike on a residential apartment in the Rimal neighborhood, west of Gaza City, early Wednesday, according to WAFA. [Footage](https://x.com/islambader_1988/status/2110258034018836861?s=46) showed a child in shock amid smoke and flames following the strike.

    * Over the past 24 hours, three Palestinians were killed--two in new Israeli attacks and one due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and 17 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.

    * The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,392 killed, with 175,440 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,501 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,323, while 838 bodies have been recovered.

  * **Israeli forces uproot olive trees, settlers attack Palestinians across the occupied West Bank:**

    * **Ramallah:** Israeli forces [uprooted](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/14/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D9%82%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%B9-%D9%85%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A3%D8%B4%D8%AC%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%AA%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%AC%D8%B1%D9%81) hundreds of productive olive trees and began leveling farmland in Kafr Malik on Wednesday, WAFA reported.

      * Near Deir Dibwan and Burqa, Israeli soldiers assaulted a Palestinian man, confiscated his vehicle, and stole his olive harvest.

    * **Nablus:** Israeli settlers attacked farmers harvesting olives in Beita, [beating and injuring](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/14/%D8%A5%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%A9-%D8%B7%D9%81%D9%84-%D8%AC%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%AA%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%8A%D9%87-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%AA%D8%A7) a 17-year-old boy. Settlers also bulldozed land in Beit Dajan to open new roads and around a family home in Burin, reportedly in preparation for a new settlement outpost.

    * **Salfit:** Settlers [attacked](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/14/%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%8A%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%AC%D9%85%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%85%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%B9%D9%8A%D9%86-%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%B1%D8%B4%D9%88%D9%86%D9%87%D9%85-%D8%A8%D8%BA%D8%A7%D8%B2) olive harvesters in Qarawat Bani Hassan with pepper spray, causing one farmer to suffer breathing difficulties.

      * Israeli forces also raided the Palestinian Prisoners Affairs Commission's office in Salfit, damaging its contents, tearing up photographs and interrogating employees.

    * **Jenin:** Israeli forces [fired tear gas](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/14/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%88%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%87-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D8%AA%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%89-%D9%85%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%B9%D9%8A%D9%86) at olive harvesters from Al-Fandaqumiya, Jaba, and Silat ad-Dhahr, forcing them off their land despite prior coordination allowing access.

      * In Ya'bad, settlers assaulted farmers, stole their olive harvest and expelled them from their land, also despite prior coordination.

    * **Bethlehem:** Israeli forces [kept](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/14/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B5%D9%84-%D8%A5%D8%BA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%82-%D8%AC%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%B9-%D9%85%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AE%D9%84-%D8%A8%D9%84%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D8%AA%D9%82%D9%88%D8%B9) all seven entrances to Tuqu' closed with iron gates for a second consecutive day, blocking other roads with earth mounds and restricting residents' access to work and essential services.

    * **Tubas:** Settlers [destroyed](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/14/%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%8A%D8%AA%D9%84%D9%81%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B4%D8%A8%D9%83%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%91-%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%B3%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B9%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AA) irrigation networks and agricultural pipelines and stole water valves and meters belonging to farmers in the northern Yarza community.

    * **Hebron:** Israeli forces [detained](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/14/%D9%85%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%AB-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D8%AA%D9%82%D9%84-8-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A8%D9%8A%D9%86%D9%87%D9%85-4-%D8%A3%D8%B7%D9%81%D8%A7%D9%84) eight Palestinians, including four children aged 14 and 15, during raids in Al-Burj, Sa'ir and Beit Ula, reportedly beating several detainees.

  * **Over 2,000 Gaza patients die awaiting medical care:** At least 2,027 patients in Gaza have [died](https://menafn.com/arabic/1111806346/%D8%A3%D8%A8%D9%88-%D8%B9%D9%81%D8%B4-%D9%88%D9%81%D8%A7%D8%A9-2027-%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%B6%D8%A7-%D8%A3%D8%AB%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%AA%D8%B8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AC-%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D8%AC%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B7%D8%A8%D9%8A-%D9%85%D9%86-%D9%82%D8%B7%D8%A7%D8%B9-%D8%BA%D8%B2%D8%A9) while awaiting treatment or medical evacuation abroad, while more than 21,000 others need evacuation, according to Mohammed Abu Afash, director of Medical Relief in Gaza.

    * Speaking to Voice of Palestine radio on Wednesday, Abu Afash said no patients had left through the Rafah crossing for more than five days, as Israel continues to close crossings and restrict medical supplies.

    * Gaza's functioning healthcare centers have fallen from more than 574 to just 227, operating with limited resources, he said.

  * **Israeli settlers torch mosque near Jerusalem amid 13 attacks on mosques in 2026:** Dozens of Israeli settlers [attacked](https://www.cwrc.ps/page-5132-ar.html) the town of Mikhmas, northeast of occupied East Jerusalem, after midnight Wednesday, setting fire to a mosque, burning a Palestinian vehicle and an olive tree, and damaging the mosque's entrance, according to the Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission.

    * The commission documented 23 incidents of arson or attempted arson targeting Palestinian mosques between January 2023 and October 11, 2026, attributing 20 to Israeli settlers and three to the Israeli military--with 13 incidents so far in 2026, accounting for more than half of all recorded cases.

    * Separately, Israeli authorities [demolished](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/14/%D8%A3%D8%A8%D9%88-%D8%AF%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%A8-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%85-%D8%A3%D9%83%D8%AB%D8%B1-%D9%85%D9%86-430-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B2%D9%84%D8%A7) more than 430 homes and structures in occupied East Jerusalem since the start of 2026, with 23,280 demolition orders outstanding and roughly 33% of Palestinian homes at risk.

  * **Gaza doctor beaten at prison in front of Israel 's Ben Gvir, Palestinian officials say: **Doctor Marwan Al-Hams, director of Gaza's field hospitals, [suffered](https://x.com/dropsitenews/status/2110266820456309160?s=46) fractures after being restrained and beaten in front of Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir at Ganot prison on October 7, according to Gaza's Health Ministry and the Prisoners' Media Office.

    * The ministry said Al-Hams was restrained, dragged and severely beaten under Ben Gvir's "direct supervision," leaving him with fractures and acute back pain. The Prisoners' Media Office called it the "harshest treatment recorded against Gaza detainees" and said he needs urgent medical care.

    * Al-Hams, a Health Ministry spokesperson, was seized by armed men in civilian clothes in Al-Mawasi on July 21, 2025, shot in the leg, and taken. Photojournalist Tamer Al-Za'anin, who was filming him for a documentary, was killed in the attack.

# Iran

  * **Three Iranian fishermen seriously injured in drone strike:** Three fishermen were seriously injured Wednesday when a fishing boat was [struck](https://en.mehrnews.com/news/248584/Drone-hit-a-boat-off-southern-Iran-port-of-Sirik-3-injured) by what local authorities described as an "enemy drone" about 18 nautical miles off Bondaran village in Sirik county, southern Iran, according to Mehr news agency.

  * **Iran reports first ship sinking from naval mine in Strait of Hormuz:** A cargo ship carrying approximately 2,500 containers [sank](https://en.irna.ir/news/86292706/Ship-carrying-2-500-containers-hits-mine-sinks-south-of-Strait) Wednesday after striking a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy said--marking the first reported sinking of a vessel caused by a mine during the war.

    * The IRGC claimed the ship was "carrying contraband" and traveling along "an unauthorized and dangerous route" in the Strait.

    * The sinking comes as Tehran reportedly [adopts](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-shifting-tactics-step-up-attacks-shipping-before-us-vote-officials-say-2026-10-14/) new tactics to increase attacks on vessels it considers in violation of its shipping restrictions, aiming to prevent Washington from lowering oil prices before November's midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters on Wednesday. Shipping attacks have reached their highest intensity since the war began, with 26 vessels hit in the last two weeks.

    * Washington has also continued enforcing its naval blockade of Iranian ports, including a Saturday strike that disabled the cargo ship Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman, according to CENTCOM.

  * **Iran carries out latest execution as UN experts call for halt:** Iran executed a man convicted of carrying out a series of shooting attacks in the southern city of Kerman that injured several civilians earlier this year, according to Iranian state broadcaster IRIB. Ali-Sina Mostafavi was hanged by Iranian authorities on Wednesday.

    * Last week, UN experts [called on](https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2026/10/iran-un-experts-urge-immediate-halt-executions-country-drives-global-surge) Iranian authorities to immediately halt all executions, warning that Iran is among a shrinking group of countries that still carries out the death penalty.

# Lebanon

  * **Israel strikes multiple towns across southern Lebanon in continued ceasefire violations:** Israeli warplanes [carried out](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/568363/%D8%BA%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%A7%D8%B7%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%81-%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AB%D8%A7-2) airstrikes on the outskirts of Hadatha in Bint Jbeil district and between Kfar Tebnit and Nabatieh Al-Fawqa in Nabatieh district on Wednesday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.

    * Israeli forces also shelled the Jallahiya area of Khiam in Marjayoun district, the outskirts of Shaqra and Wadi Al-Salouqi in Bint Jbeil district.

  * **UN warns Israeli attacks and destruction in southern Lebanon may amount to war crimes despite ceasefire:** The UN Human Rights Office [expressed](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/568402/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D9%85%D9%85-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%AA%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D9%84%D8%AD%D9%82%D9%88%D9%82-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D9%86%D8%B3%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%AA%D8%AD%D8%B0%D9%91%D8%B1-%D9%85%D9%86-%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA%D9%85%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%87%D8%AC%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D9%88%D8%AA%D9%81%D8%A7%D9%82%D9%85-%D9%85%D8%B9%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%AF%D9%86%D9%8A%D9%8A%D9%86-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D9%84%D8%A8%D9%86%D8%A7%D9%86-2) "grave concern" over continued Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon despite the ceasefire, citing recent airstrikes, drone attacks, shelling, and explosions across several districts.

    * It warned that Israeli forces continue to destroy homes, schools, healthcare facilities, water networks, and farmland in occupied areas of southern Lebanon, leaving entire villages and towns nearly wiped out and preventing thousands of displaced residents from returning.

    * The UN said these actions constitute widespread violations of international humanitarian law, some of which may amount to war crimes or other crimes under international law.

    * At least 4,387 people, including at least 660 women and children and 135 healthcare workers, were killed between March 2 and October 11, 2026, with another 12,424 injured, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry.

# U.S. News

  * **Top House Republicans privately concede House control is "all but gone," shift focus to saving Senate majority**: Five senior Republican lawmakers speaking anonymously to Politico [said](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/14/house-republicans-private-lost-cause-01117673) that the House has all but slipped away from the GOP, and that the party's goal is now to limit the scale of the defeat and hold the Senate. One senior House Republican said the aim is to "save as many Republican seats as we can," adding that "President Trump has made this election all about himself. Now we have to survive that political storm." A second lawmaker predicted Democrats would pick up about 10 seats, more than enough for a majority, and said even in newly redistricted Florida and Texas, Republican candidates are "hanging on with their fingernails."

  * **Federal probe of Rep. Ilhan Omar reportedly centers on birth date and citizenship papers** : The Department of Justice investigation that led agents to search the Washington residence of **Rep. Ilhan Omar** (D-Minn.) Monday [focuses](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/10/13/rep-omar-investigation-focuses-birthdate-citizenship-papers-people-familiar-say/) on claims that she or her late father may have lied on decades-old immigration paperwork to secure legal status and eventually citizenship, the Washington Post reported. Omar, whose family fled Somalia and immigrated to the U.S. in 1995, has repeatedly rejected the allegations, calling them "baseless lies and smear campaigns" and the latest attempt by the administration "to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement."

    * DOJ has filed at least 163 denaturalization cases since January 2025, including 40 since August, versus about 11 a year from 1990 to 2017. Such cases rarely reach decades-old conduct outside serious transnational crimes.

  * **DOJ gives California 48 hours to act on alleged noncitizen voter list or face legal action** : In a Tuesday letter to California Secretary of State **Shirley Weber** , [reviewed](https://www.reuters.com/world/us-justice-department-threatens-california-over-alleged-noncitizen-voters-letter-2026-10-14/) by Reuters, acting Deputy Attorney **General R. Trent McCotter** demanded the state take a series of actions related to a list of voters until their citizenship is confirmed, including segregating any returned ballots, or face legal action.

    * The letter escalates the administration's pressure on states and suggests DOJ may challenge ballots before the Nov. 3 election. DOJ has repeatedly claimed noncitizen voting is widespread despite studies showing it is rare. DOJ's Civil Rights Division has sued 30 states that refused to hand over voter data and has lost 26 cases without a win.

  * **NYC Comptroller Mark Levine backs off campaign pledge to buy Israeli bonds:** New York City Comptroller **Mark Levine** said on Wednesday he and his investment team decided not to buy bonds from the state of Israel, the New York Times [reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/14/nyregion/mark-levine-comptroller-israel.html), reversing a campaign promise. He said the call was made "entirely on financial grounds," citing "some technical challenges" and an "ongoing" analysis. Levine, a vocal supporter of Israel, said that, given regional instability and his office's preference for shorter-term bonds, reinvesting made little sense.

  * **ICE seeks AI software to monitor detainees ' calls, video and movements**: ICE [posted](https://www.washingtonsun.com/immigration/ice-ai-monitor-detainees) a request for information Friday on a federal contracting website seeking AI software to use transcription and voice recognition to monitor detainees' calls, along with data from detention-center cameras, the Washington Sun reported on Tuesday. The system would run 24/7 and store detainee profiles.

    * ICE already monitors calls not related to detainees' legal cases, but voice recognition would significantly expand its capacity. The software would track whether the person on a call matches the one associated with the dialed number, labeling mismatches "receiver-side deception."

  * **Trump pardons two Alaska mechanics on stage at Wasilla rally:** Trump [pardoned](https://www.washingtonsun.com/whitehouse/trump-alaska-pardons-mechanics) Alaska mechanics **Zachary Czubak** and **Patrick Fleming** at a Tuesday rally in Wasilla, clearing them of guilty pleas for violating the Clean Air Act.
